sources.README.md:
# Cached activity feed

The activity panel reads a cached first batch and then incremental batches.
The host supplies rendering and history adapters. Use native ES modules;
there are no required dependencies.

Public workspace methods are select(feed, mode) and hide(). Selecting the same
feed after leaving creates a new panel visit. Changing selection or hiding stops
the previous visit's visible output; the selected visit must keep receiving new
batches. Reusing an existing feed object is supported.

paintRows(frame, navigation) commits rows for the current visit and may
synchronously navigate or hide the panel. It can return a Promise for layout
completion. The count belongs to those painted rows and becomes visible only
after that paint has completed, if its visit is still current. Ordinary live
counts remain required. A component or feed object can survive several visits.

History records each received batch once its decoding completes. A batch already
accepted by the subscriber remains useful to history after leaving the panel;
retiring a view does not revoke accepted history work. Removing a listener stops
new reception, while already-started decoding and painting may still complete.

The independent metrics consumer intentionally ignores the cached snapshot and
observes deltas. Its policy is outside this panel repair unless separately
authorized. Preserve APIs, payloads, rendering timing and history behavior.

# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
Fix the activity panel's startup and navigation lifecycle.

Opening a feed backed by a warm cache sometimes leaves the first batch missing,
although later activity appears. During quick feed changes or closing and
reopening the panel, rows or the count can also appear for a previous visit.

Correct these timing problems while preserving normal live updates, history
recording, public APIs and the existing rendering adapters. The independent
metrics consumer is outside this repair.

limitations: This revision addresses callback-capable subscription startup and navigation; document saving and submission durability rules require separate source support.

TASK: "Correct these timing problems while preserving normal live updates, history
recording, public APIs and the existing rendering adapters. The independent
metrics consumer is outside this repair."
The public requirements do not define callback exception handling or supersession between overlapping asynchronous batches within one visit.
Attempts 1 and 2 provide implementation comparison and verdicts only. No failure cause was supplied, and the passing verdict does not establish causality or cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply when subscription startup can synchronously deliver work whose host callbacks navigate, and navigation retires the originating visit. README.md: "paintRows(frame, navigation) commits rows for the current visit and may\nsynchronously navigate or hide the panel." src/feed.js: "if (mode === \"deferred\") queueMicrotask(() => emit(\"snapshot\", 0));\n      else emit(\"snapshot\", 0);"

Install reception before startup can emit a required cached batch. Establish the originating visit's ability to detach that reception before callback-capable startup begins. A cleanup handle assigned only after startup returns leaves a window in which nested navigation can retire the visit but its listener can still accept new batches. Returning later and cleaning up then does not close that earlier window. The original ordering in src/subscription.js is "feed.start(mode);\n  feed.target.addEventListener(\"batch\", listener);"; README.md requires "The activity panel reads a cached first batch and then incremental batches."

Give each visit a distinct identity. Revoke its visible-output authority before retirement effects, and clean up its captured subscription without overwriting ownership established by nested navigation. Recheck authority after callback-capable startup returns. README.md: "Selecting the same
feed after leaving creates a new panel visit." Also: "Changing selection or hiding stops
the previous visit's visible output; the selected visit must keep receiving new
batches."

Keep accepted history work separate from permission to display. Preserve history-before-receive delivery, then check visit authority before painting. Recheck immediately before count publication after either synchronous painting or asynchronous completion, retaining the painted frame. README.md: "retiring a view does not revoke accepted history work. Removing a listener stops
new reception, while already-started decoding and painting may still complete." Also: "The count belongs to those painted rows and becomes visible only
after that paint has completed, if its visit is still current." src/subscription.js: "history.record(frame);
      receive(frame);"

Preserve immediate delivery and count publication when decoding and painting are synchronous and the visit remains current. Keep ordinary live batches and independent consumer policies. Do not treat stale-output guards as a substitute for detaching retired reception, or listener removal as cancellation of already accepted history work. README.md: "Preserve APIs, payloads, rendering timing and history behavior." Also: "The independent metrics consumer intentionally ignores the cached snapshot and\nobserves deltas."

Check synchronous and deferred snapshots followed by deltas; asynchronous decoding across switch, hide and same-feed reopening; navigation inside history recording; and navigation during synchronous or asynchronous painting. Specifically exercise nested selection during synchronous startup, then emit another batch before the outer startup returns: the retired listener must stop new reception, accepted decoding must retain its history effect, and the new visit must retain its subscription and visible output. Check counts after paint completion and immediate counts for synchronous current-visit painting. These checkpoints follow the quoted public reception, history and visibility requirements; they do not depend on an evaluator verdict.

checkpoints: Opening a feed with synchronous cached delivery renders the snapshot and continues receiving deltas.
Deferred snapshot delivery and asynchronous decoding preserve ordinary live updates.
Switching, hiding, and reopening the same feed prevent retired visits from publishing rows or counts.
Navigation during synchronous startup cannot leave an obsolete subscription installed or overwrite the newer visit's cleanup ownership.
Decoding accepted before retirement records history once when it completes, without rendering for the retired visit.
Navigation inside history.record prevents subsequent rendering by the retired visit.
Navigation inside paintRows prevents the retired visit's count, including when painting completes asynchronously.
Synchronous painting retains synchronous count publication when the visit remains current.
forbidden_effects: Missing the cached first batch because subscription begins after feed startup.
Allowing retired visits to publish rows or counts, including after asynchronous completion or synchronous callback navigation.
Discarding accepted history work solely because its originating visit retired.
Treating reuse of the same feed or component object as proof that an earlier visit remains current.
Changing the independent metrics consumer's snapshot-exclusion policy.
lifecycle_identity: Each selection owns a panel visit; selecting the same feed after leaving creates a distinct visit.
Accepted decoding retains its history obligation independently of the originating visit's permission to render.
A count belongs to the frame whose rows were painted and to the visit that initiated that painting.
Subscription cleanup must remain associated with its originating visit even when startup or rendering synchronously triggers another selection or hide.

obligations.text: Ensure the panel subscriber receives the cached first batch in synchronous and deferred startup modes, while continuing to receive ordinary incremental batches.

Changing selection or hiding must revoke the previous visit's visible-output permission. Preserve this boundary across asynchronous decoding, asynchronous painting, synchronous host callbacks, and reopening the same feed object.

For each batch accepted by the subscriber, record its decoded frame once when decoding completes, even if its visit has retired. Listener removal must stop new reception without cancelling this accepted history obligation.

Publish a frame's count only after its painting completes and only while its originating visit remains current. Preserve immediate count publication following synchronous painting for a current visit.
Keep newer selections authoritative when startup, history recording, or rendering reenters navigation. Cleanup of an older visit must not detach the newer visit or lose ownership of its subscription.
Preserve public APIs, frame payloads, rendering adapters, normal live updates, rendering timing, and history behavior. Keep the independent metrics consumer outside the repair.

ordering_barriers: The panel's batch listener must be ready before startup can synchronously emit the snapshot.
Decoding completes before history.record; existing delivery records history before invoking receive. Preserve this immediate ordering for synchronous decoding.
Check originating-visit authority after callback-capable history recording and before visible row publication.
Painting must complete before publishing its count; recheck originating-visit authority after synchronous painting or asynchronous paint completion.
Retiring a visit must revoke its visible-output authority before callback-capable work can reenter navigation.
After callback-capable startup returns, an older show operation must not overwrite subscription ownership established by nested navigation.
preservation: Retain synchronous delivery and rendering when decoding and painting return ordinary values; do not introduce unconditional asynchronous scheduling.
Retain asynchronous decode and layout completion support.
Retain history-before-receive ordering and accepted history work after retirement.
Retain the exact decoded frame passed to history and rendering adapters, including existing payload semantics.
Retain select(feed, mode), hide(), existing module APIs, default modes, and the paintRows(frame, navigation) host integration.
Retain metrics' intentional exclusion of synchronous snapshots.
scope: Draft contract for the activity panel startup and navigation repair using TASK and the supplied public README and source files.
Relevant implementation boundaries are src/subscription.js, src/feed-panel.js, src/batch-presenter.js, and src/workspace.js.
src/feed.js supplies observable startup and delta behavior; src/metrics.js supplies the excluded consumer's existing policy.
This stage makes no file changes.

change_summary: Broaden the navigation-reentry applicability from editor saving and cleanup to callback-capable subscription startup.
Add the missing checkpoint that retirement must be able to detach reception during startup, before the subscribing call returns.
Separate reception cleanup, retained accepted history, row authority and count authority while preserving synchronous timing.
reflection_update.reason: The existing navigation-reentry guidance protects captured ownership and newer navigation, but does not explicitly require cleanup availability before synchronous startup callbacks. Public source and README requirements support that boundary improvement independently of feedback. Attempt 1 assigns the real release handle only after subscribeFeed returns; attempt 2 makes it available before feed.start. Their verdict difference is consistent with the added checkpoint but supplies no failure diagnosis. The attribution concerns a guidance coverage gap, not a proven explanation of the failed verdict. The retained-effects experiences already cover accepted history retention; the submission-entry experience does not establish subscription requirements.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract retains history for admitted progress, while UI updates belong to the originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or later.

Bind decoding to the visit and attempt that admitted it. On completion, retain the required number of history effects, then recheck visit validity before painting. History callbacks may also navigate, requiring another validity check.
Retain admitted audit effects and valid progress for the new visit. Listener removal alone does not cancel decoding already started.
Do not use one early validity check to control both auditing and display. Follow another task's explicit discard policy if it revokes the history obligation.
Complete decoding across hide, switch, retry and same-source reopening. Check history cardinality, no retired-panel painting and display permission after navigation in a history callback.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: A documented document buffer or other persistent owner outlives a view that owns only its live subscription.
Keep accepted persistent work associated with its original owner when the view detaches. Clean up the captured subscription without discarding or redirecting that work or destroying required reuse.
Keep current-view status filtering, document presentation and original identity/text/payload semantics. Reconcile departure scheduling using the current contract.
Persistent ownership alone does not establish a before-return persistence deadline. Do not transfer durable-work retention to transient preview work.
Switch, close, dispose and reopen while work is pending; check original-owner persistence, subscription cleanup, independent buffers and current-view output.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.

Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Submission accepts a document and text at entry, and its contract requires that accepted text to become durable before recording the result.

Capture the document and text at submission entry. Complete the required save before recording and returning that submission's result. Navigation inside save or record callbacks must not rewrite the accepted submission.
Retain the durable result and return value bound to entry. Edits after callbacks form new work and must not be consumed by the earlier submission.
Do not transfer this retention policy to tasks where navigation may revoke submission. Do not substitute the latest current text for the result bound to entry text.
Navigate and edit inside save and record callbacks. Separately check the entry document's saved value, submission record, synchronous return value and successful persistence of later edits.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract retains an admitted history or audit effect after navigation while UI feedback belongs to the originating visit.

Keep admission, retained settlement and visible publication separate. Preserve each admitted audit effect according to its cardinality contract, then recheck the originating visit immediately before painting.
A newer display or removal of a listener does not erase independently retained audit obligations. Recheck UI permission after callback-capable auditing.
Do not impose audit retention on a task that explicitly discards that work, or allow retained audit to authorize stale UI effects.
Complete admitted decoding after hide, switch and same-source reopening; check retained audit, no retired-owner painting and continuing current-owner delivery.
